description: I am a robotics enthusiast interested in people who want to create both a physical and a software project related to the selected challenge.
summary: Astro Pulse is an integrated hardware-and-software health monitoring system designed specifically for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Powered by an ESP32 microcontroller paired with real-time heart rate (MAX30102) and surface temperature (MLX90614) sensors, our solution streams live biometric data to a custom Python FastAPI dashboard. Beyond instant readings, the system automatically logs monitoring sessions, generates CSV reports, and tracks long-term physiological trends using interactive trend charts. By bridging real-time telemetry with historical health analytics, Astro Pulse gives astronauts and flight surgeons an intuitive, reliable tool to monitor and protect their well-being in space.
details:
What does it do and how does it work? Astro Pulse is an end-to-end vital signs monitoring and analytics ecosystem built for astronauts on space missions. Using a custom hardware unit powered by an ESP32 microcontroller, the device captures real-time heart rate (BPM) via a MAX30102 pulse sensor and non-contact surface and ambient temperature via an MLX90614 infrared sensor. Physical push-buttons allow the user to toggle between monitoring modes effortlessly, displaying live readings on a built-in round GC9A01A TFT screen. Simultaneously, the ESP32 streams this telemetry over USB Serial to a Python FastAPI backend. The software validates incoming readings, evaluates physiological thresholds (such as detecting bradycardia, tachycardia, or elevated fever ranges), logs complete sessions into downloadable CSV files, and displays real-time data and historical trend charts on a web dashboard.

What benefits does it have?

  • Dual-Display and Offline Resilience: Astronauts get instant visual feedback directly on the handheld TFT display without needing to look at a computer, while automatically syncing detailed analytics when connected to the dashboard.
  • Automated Health Insights: Rather than displaying raw numbers alone, the system computes session statistics (mean, median, minimum, maximum) and provides immediate threshold status alerts on both the hardware screen and web interface.
  • Long-Term Trend Tracking: The web dashboard automatically categorizes past sessions and renders interactive tendency charts, making it easy to spot gradual physiological changes over weeks or months in space.

What is the intended impact of the project? Long-duration spaceflight places extreme stress on the human cardiovascular and thermoregulatory systems. Astro Pulse aims to empower astronauts with autonomous, easy-to-use self-monitoring tools while providing flight surgeons with structured, longitudinal health logs. By bridging instant point-of-care checks with multi-session trend analytics, it enables early detection of physiological drift before minor anomalies become critical medical emergencies in deep space.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Hardware: ESP32 microcontroller, MAX30102 heart rate and pulse sensor, MLX90614 non-contact infrared temperature sensor, GC9A01A 1.28-inch round TFT LCD display, and tactile push-buttons.
  • Firmware and Embedded Software: C++ (Arduino IDE), Wire (I2C), SPI, ArduinoJson, Adafruit_GFX, Adafruit_GC9A01A, Adafruit_MLX90614, and SparkFun MAX3010x libraries.
  • Backend and Web Dashboard: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, PySerial, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Chart.js for rendering interactive historical tendency graphs.

How is your project creative? Instead of building a purely software-based concept or a basic raw sensor readout, we created a two-way serial communication loop between custom hardware and a web analytics engine. Not only does the ESP32 send live sensor data to Python, but the Python backend also processes session statistics, evaluates health thresholds, and sends a formatted JSON summary back to the ESP32 to display health status results directly on the round TFT screen.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Sensor Calibration and Hardware Reliability: We accounted for surface-temperature displacement on the MLX90614 sensor by calibrating the fever evaluation threshold (41°C) to prevent false alarms, configured I2C bus speeds (100kHz) to avoid sensor lockups, and added software debouncing and startup lockouts to physical buttons so accidental bumps in microgravity do not trigger false sessions.
  • Usability in High-Stress Environments: We designed a high-contrast, dark-mode web interface and a clutter-free round display layout (showing only essential numbers and clear status alerts) so crew members can read their vitals at a glance.
  • Data Portability: By storing sessions in standardized CSV formats alongside automatic chart generation, crew members can easily reset, export, or share data logs with medical teams on Earth.
